title: AI Batch generating TRILLIONS of different MT5 Expert advisors w/validation
author: tommytradez
selftext:
This platform solved the problem that rules out most hosted EA builders. It never gets your broker login. There is no API key field and nowhere to put one, and no live strategy of yours ever runs on their servers. What you get instead is a file. An MQL5 Expert Advisor that runs in your own MetaTrader 5, on your machine, with your broker.

Everything else follows from that.

**Up to 100 strategies in seconds** Different indicators, entry and exit logic, timeframes, stops and sizing, not variations of one idea. Indicators × parameter ranges × conditions × timeframes × risk models is an effectively unbounded space, and the point is searching it rather than hand-tuning one config until the curve looks good.

**Costs modelled per symbol.** Spread, commission and swap, not one flat number

**Safety rails, applied to every strategy**

* **Weekend flatten.** Closes positions 15 minutes before the Friday close (16:45 New York). It follows the DST change rather than sitting at a fixed UTC hour, so it lands 15 minutes before the close all year.
* **Rollover window.** No entries or exits between 21:00 and 22:00 UTC, when spreads blow out and stops get speared. Deferred exits fire at the real post-window price.
* **Max spread.** Blocks new entries above N times normal for that symbol. On EURUSD 5x is about 1.5 pips against 0.3 normal, on gold about 16 against 3.3. Exits are never blocked, so stops and targets always run.

**Parity with MT5, published in full:** [**https://roboticea.com/parity-study**](https://roboticea.com/parity-study)

100 EURUSD strategies run twice, once through their own C++ engine and once through the MT5 Strategy Tester, off the same 24.6 million real tick stream, with matched costs on both sides, February to December 2023.

* 62% within 5% on trade count (71% for ordinary entry and exit strategies)
* median trade-count gap 3.8%, median return gap 6.1 percentage points
* all 100 rows are on the page, including the ones that disagree and why

These are test returns, not achievable ones. Nothing here is financial advice.
